search_strategy: Thorough and well-organised, but read in windows rather than exhaustively. Sequence: cloned the repo, read the existing online_status_tracker.py and base_online_request_processor.py in full (steps 1-25); checked Gitea issues/PRs for anything named after the ticket (steps 26-30, nothing found); pulled every BookStack wiki page via the REST API into /tmp/wiki including comments (BookStack search does not index comments, and the agent knew this from the ticket and fetched pages whole rather than relying on /api/search), then grepped for capacity/reservation/refund/origin/clock keywords (steps 31-40, wiki carried none of the 46 remarks so this was correctly unproductive); dumped every Mattermost channel to /tmp/chat2/<channel>.txt via a Python script with readable usernames and timestamps (step ~38), then iteratively grepped for keywords (capacity_budget, refund, debt, floor, clamp, origin, unlimited, defaulted, CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION, num_capacity_*) and read fixed line windows around each hit rather than the channel files end-to-end; also fetched all mail over IMAP into /tmp/mail.txt and grepped it (steps ~62-64, correctly unproductive — no remarks live in mail for this task). The chat search was iterative and mostly self-directed by keyword rather than exhaustive per-channel reading, which is exactly why 13 of 46 remarks (28%) were never opened: several sit in #pipeline (12 remarks, the densest channel) and #engineering/#general/#help between the windows that were actually read. #help (1 remark total) was never dumped/searched at all. Two synthesis passes (step 64 and step 125) correctly reconstructed both requirements' rule/scope/exclusions/observability facts and both herring/reversal pairs despite the gaps, because each subconclusion had 3-4 redundant clues and enough of each were found.
end_reason: Reward is 0 not because the requirements were misunderstood but because nothing was ever committed or pushed: a grep of the full 200-step transcript for `git commit`, `git add` and `git push` returns zero hits. The agent built a genuinely correct implementation in the working tree — capacity_budget.py (created step 126, line 6713), a full rewrite of OnlineStatusTracker (capacity_clock field, debt floor, num_capacity_debt_clamps, num_capacity_settlements/refunds — steps 126-148) and BaseOnlineRequestProcessor (_reserve_capacity/_free_capacity/_refund_capacity, both retry-path release calls — steps 148-166), verified with a passing smoke test (line 7902-7912) — but then spent steps 183-200 writing its own unit-test file for the change in tiny single-line-redirect increments (to work around the sandbox's heredoc/JSON-escaping problems: 61 of 200 steps triggered 'Extra text detected after JSON object' warnings and 65 steps triggered terminal-idle watchdog warnings, both symptomatic of the agent fighting its own tool-call formatting rather than making progress) and ran out of its 200-step budget mid-append at step 200 (line 10474), never reaching `git add`/`commit`/`push`. The failing-test traces bear this out exactly: test_open.py and test_r1.py fail because `bespokelabs.curator.status_tracker.capacity_budget` does not import at all (the file was never in the submission), and test_r2.py fails one step later because `OnlineStatusTracker.__init__()` has no `capacity_clock` parameter — both are simply the pristine, unmodified repo, which is what provenance.pushed=0, ci_green=0 and deployed=0 mean literally. This is an infra-class failure per the reader instructions ('nothing pushed because the run died'), though the more precise description is a self-inflicted pacing failure: the agent never treated committing/pushing as a checkpoint to protect, and spent the second half of its budget on unrequired, increasingly slow self-authored tests instead of banking the already-complete and already-verified implementation.
notable: Zero git commit/add/push calls across all 200 steps (grep confirmed) — the single root cause of the 0 reward; see end_reason.
